conversation_context.content: I'm instrumenting a Python agent by hand. How can I attach env='staging' to just one turn in its trace?

Call `set_attributes()` on that turn's `Turn` object while the turn is open. This stamps the attributes on that one turn span. [S1]

```python
import weave

weave.init("[TEAM-NAME]/[PROJECT-NAME]")

with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="my-agent"):
    with weave.start_turn(user_message="What is the weather in Tokyo?") as turn:
        turn.set_attributes({"env": "staging"})
```

This pattern comes from the docs' example, which sets `"env": "production"` on a turn. [S1]

**Details**
- `set_attributes()` takes a dictionary and returns the span, so you can chain calls. [S1]
- Call it while the span is recording, which means inside the `with` block. If you call it on a span that hasn't started or has already ended, it does nothing and logs a warning. [S3]
- `env` is a custom key, so Weave stores it as a filterable custom attribute. Weave reserves the `weave.*` and `gen_ai.*` prefixes for special handling, so don't use those prefixes for this. [S1]
- The same method exists on the other span types (`LLM`, `Tool`, `SubAgent`). Use it there if you want only a tool call or LLM call tagged, not the whole turn. [S1][S2]

**Caveats**
- The docs also describe conversation-wide attributes that apply to every span a conversation emits. Avoid those if you want just one turn tagged. [S2] I didn't read that section, so I can't give its details.
- If you log finished turns in a batch with `log_turn` or `log_conversation`, the docs say to populate the span object's declared fields and pass the object in. [S3] The `log_conversation` reference says its `attributes` argument is stamped on every emitted span. That makes it the wrong tool for tagging a single turn. I only saw a truncated snippet of that reference.

**Next step:** add the `turn.set_attributes({"env": "staging"})` line to the turn you want tagged. Then filter on `env` in the Weights & Biases UI. The docs have a "View and filter attributes in the UI" section, but I didn't read it.

Pass `attributes` once to `startConversation`. You don't need to repeat it on each LLM or tool span. [S4]

```typescript
import * as weave from 'weave';

await weave.init('[TEAM-NAME]/[PROJECT-NAME]');

const conversation = weave.startConversation({
  agentName: 'my-agent',
  attributes: { env: 'production' },
});
```

The docs say this applies the attributes to every span the conversation emits. Their example comment lists the turn, LLM, tool and sub-agent spans. [S4] The `ConversationInit` reference describes `attributes` as custom attributes propagated to every span the conversation emits. [S5]

**Caveats**
- **Key names:** `env` is a custom key, which is what the docs recommend. Avoid the reserved `gen_ai.*` and `weave.*` prefixes. Weave extracts those into typed fields during ingestion, so a custom value under a reserved key is unsupported. [S4]
- **Typed fields:** set the agent name, conversation name and model through their typed parameters, not through `attributes`. [S4] In TypeScript, `agentName` is one of those parameters. [S4]
- **Collisions:** if a key collides with a span's own `gen_ai.*` or `weave.*` attribute, the span's value wins. [S5]
- **No conversation:** `TurnInit` also has an `attributes` option. It is meant for a rootless `startTurn({ attributes })` with no conversation, and it passes the attributes to child spans. [S6] You don't need it when you start a conversation.
- **Per-span extras:** to add something to one span only, use `setAttributes()` on that span. [S4]
- **Not covered:** I didn't read the page's "When you can set attributes" section. I also didn't confirm how `startTurn` finds the current conversation in your code, so check that the turn runs inside the conversation you started.

**Correction to my earlier answer:** that was Python-specific. For TypeScript, the per-span method is `setAttributes()`, not `set_attributes()`. [S4]

# Set attributes and events on agent spans

> Attach custom attributes and record events on agent spans (Turn, LLM, Tool, and SubAgent) to filter and analyze agent activity in Weave.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/attributes-and-events).

When you instrument an agent with the Weave SDK, each span object (`Turn`, `LLM`, `Tool`, and `SubAgent`) exposes methods to attach custom metadata. Use these methods to stamp contextual information such as user IDs, tenants, experiment names, or environment labels onto agent spans, then filter and group agent activity by that metadata in the Weights & Biases UI.

This metadata comes in two forms:

* **Attributes**: Key-value properties of a span as a whole. Use `set_attributes()` (Python) or `setAttributes()` (TypeScript) to stamp attributes on a single span, or set conversation-wide attributes that apply to every span a conversation emits.
* **Events**: Point-in-time markers that occur during a span's lifetime, such as a permission prompt or a lifecycle transition. Use `add_event()` (Python) or `addEvent()` (TypeScript).

These methods mirror the [OpenTelemetry (OTel) span API](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-spans/): `set_attributes` mirrors OTel's `Span.set_attributes`, and `add_event` mirrors OTel's `Span.add_event`. The Weave SDK emits OTel spans and stores all attributes, so they remain queryable in Weave.

all_read_evidence.text:
## When you can set attributes

Set attributes while the span is recording, that is, after the span starts and before it ends. In Python, this is inside the `with` block. In TypeScript, this is after `start*()` and before `end()`.

If you call `set_attributes()`, or its TypeScript equivalent on a span that hasn't started yet or has already ended, the call is a no-op and logs a warning that names the fix.

The call is silent (no warning) only when OTel isn't installed or Weave is disabled.

> [!TIP]
>
> To attach attributes when logging completed agent activity in a single batch rather than during live execution, populate the span object's declared fields directly and pass the object to `log_turn` or `log_conversation`. See [Log agent activity in batches](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents-batch.md).

This metadata comes in two forms:

## When you can set attributes

Set attributes while the span is recording, that is, after the span starts and before it ends. In Python, this is inside the `with` block. In TypeScript, this is after `start*()` and before `end()`.

If you call `set_attributes()`, or its TypeScript equivalent on a span that hasn't started yet or has already ended, the call is a no-op and logs a warning that names the fix.

The call is silent (no warning) only when OTel isn't installed or Weave is disabled.

> [!TIP]
>
> To attach attributes when logging completed agent activity in a single batch rather than during live execution, populate the span object's declared fields directly and pass the object to `log_turn` or `log_conversation`. See [Log agent activity in batches](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents-batch.md).

Weave supports attribute conventions from the following observability frameworks and SDKs:

* **OpenLit**: OpenLit observability attributes (`gen_ai.content.completion`).
* **Logfire / Pydantic AI**: Logfire's Pydantic AI instrumentation (`gen_ai.input.messages`, `gen_ai.output.messages`, `pydantic_ai.all_messages`, `final_result`).

turns.answer:
Pass `attributes` once to `startConversation`. You don't need to repeat it on each LLM or tool span. [S4]

```typescript
import * as weave from 'weave';

await weave.init('[TEAM-NAME]/[PROJECT-NAME]');

const conversation = weave.startConversation({
  agentName: 'my-agent',
  attributes: { env: 'production' },
});
```

The docs say this applies the attributes to every span the conversation emits. Their example comment lists the turn, LLM, tool and sub-agent spans. [S4] The `ConversationInit` reference describes `attributes` as custom attributes propagated to every span the conversation emits. [S5]

**Caveats**
- **Key names:** `env` is a custom key, which is what the docs recommend. Avoid the reserved `gen_ai.*` and `weave.*` prefixes. Weave extracts those into typed fields during ingestion, so a custom value under a reserved key is unsupported. [S4]
- **Typed fields:** set the agent name, conversation name and model through their typed parameters, not through `attributes`. [S4] In TypeScript, `agentName` is one of those parameters. [S4]
- **Collisions:** if a key collides with a span's own `gen_ai.*` or `weave.*` attribute, the span's value wins. [S5]
- **No conversation:** `TurnInit` also has an `attributes` option. It is meant for a rootless `startTurn({ attributes })` with no conversation, and it passes the attributes to child spans. [S6] You don't need it when you start a conversation.
- **Per-span extras:** to add something to one span only, use `setAttributes()` on that span. [S4]
- **Not covered:** I didn't read the page's "When you can set attributes" section. I also didn't confirm how `startTurn` finds the current conversation in your code, so check that the turn runs inside the conversation you started.

# Set attributes and events on agent spans

> Attach custom attributes and record events on agent spans (Turn, LLM, Tool, and SubAgent) to filter and analyze agent activity in Weave.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/attributes-and-events).

When you instrument an agent with the Weave SDK, each span object (`Turn`, `LLM`, `Tool`, and `SubAgent`) exposes methods to attach custom metadata. Use these methods to stamp contextual information such as user IDs, tenants, experiment names, or environment labels onto agent spans, then filter and group agent activity by that metadata in the Weights & Biases UI.

This metadata comes in two forms:

* **Attributes**: Key-value properties of a span as a whole. Use `set_attributes()` (Python) or `setAttributes()` (TypeScript) to stamp attributes on a single span, or set conversation-wide attributes that apply to every span a conversation emits.
* **Events**: Point-in-time markers that occur during a span's lifetime, such as a permission prompt or a lifecycle transition. Use `add_event()` (Python) or `addEvent()` (TypeScript).

These methods mirror the [OpenTelemetry (OTel) span API](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-spans/): `set_attributes` mirrors OTel's `Span.set_attributes`, and `add_event` mirrors OTel's `Span.add_event`. The Weave SDK emits OTel spans and stores all attributes, so they remain queryable in Weave.

Pass `attributes` once to `startConversation`. You don't need to repeat it on each LLM or tool span. [S4]

```typescript
import * as weave from 'weave';

await weave.init('[TEAM-NAME]/[PROJECT-NAME]');

const conversation = weave.startConversation({
  agentName: 'my-agent',
  attributes: { env: 'production' },
});
```

The docs say this applies the attributes to every span the conversation emits. Their example comment lists the turn, LLM, tool and sub-agent spans. [S4] The `ConversationInit` reference describes `attributes` as custom attributes propagated to every span the conversation emits. [S5]

**Caveats**
- **Key names:** `env` is a custom key, which is what the docs recommend. Avoid the reserved `gen_ai.*` and `weave.*` prefixes. Weave extracts those into typed fields during ingestion, so a custom value under a reserved key is unsupported. [S4]
- **Typed fields:** set the agent name, conversation name and model through their typed parameters, not through `attributes`. [S4] In TypeScript, `agentName` is one of those parameters. [S4]
- **Collisions:** if a key collides with a span's own `gen_ai.*` or `weave.*` attribute, the span's value wins. [S5]
- **No conversation:** `TurnInit` also has an `attributes` option. It is meant for a rootless `startTurn({ attributes })` with no conversation, and it passes the attributes to child spans. [S6] You don't need it when you start a conversation.
- **Per-span extras:** to add something to one span only, use `setAttributes()` on that span. [S4]
- **Not covered:** I didn't read the page's "When you can set attributes" section. I also didn't confirm how `startTurn` finds the current conversation in your code, so check that the turn runs inside the conversation you started.

**Correction to my earlier answer:** that was Python-specific. For TypeScript, the per-span method is `setAttributes()`, not `set_attributes()`. [S4]

**Next step:** add `attributes: { env: 'production' }` to your existing `startConversation` call. Then check that an LLM or tool span carries `env`.
